claude.sample_unit: patients (HPSCC; reader study on 51 cases with 6 radiation oncologists)

links.outcome: Reader contouring DSC, time, and consistency with versus without AI assistance in randomized crossover
links.effect: AI assistance increased mean DSC in juniors from 0.73 to 0.86 and seniors from 0.79 to 0.84, reduced contouring time by 55%, improved Fleiss' κ from 0.69 to 0.86 (all p < 0.01).
links.quote: In the reader study, AI assistance increased mean DSC in juniors from 0.73 ± 0.16 to 0.86 ± 0.14 and in seniors from 0.79 ± 0.13 to 0.84 ± 0.15, reduced contouring time by 55%, and improved Fleiss' κ from 0.69 ± 0.12 to 0.86 ± 0.12 (all p < 0.01).

links.outcome: Model segmentation DSC across internal and two external sites
links.effect: Mean DSC 0.87 ± 0.11 internally and 0.85 ± 0.14 and 0.82 ± 0.16 in external cohorts; risk model AUC 0.89 internally vs 0.71-0.78 externally.
links.quote: Tri-sequence mean DSC was 0.87 ± 0.11 internally and 0.85 ± 0.14 and 0.82 ± 0.16 in external cohorts.

unlisted_practices: MRI quality-feature-based prediction of low-overlap auto-segmentation cases to support deployment

Quality-aware low-overlap risk modeling using MRI-quality features and auto-segmentation-derived tumor volume to flag likely segmentation failures.

screen.practice: AI-assisted contouring with clinician review vs manual contouring
screen.reason: The study conducts a randomized crossover reader study evaluating AI-assisted vs manual contouring by junior and senior oncologists (human-in-the-loop assistance) and evaluates an exploratory deployment-support low-overlap risk model to detect poor-quality segmentation.

primary.practice: AI-assisted contouring vs manual clinician workflow and low-overlap quality risk modeling
